records.source: וַיְהִי֩ בִשְׁנַ֨ת הַתְּשִׁיעִ֜ית לְמָלְכ֗וֹ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָעֲשִׂירִי֮ בֶּעָשׂ֣וֹר לַחֹדֶשׁ֒ בָּ֠א נְבֻכַדְנֶאצַּ֨ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֜ל ה֧וּא וְכָל־חֵיל֛וֹ עַל־יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם וַיִּ֣חַן עָלֶ֑יהָ וַיִּבְנ֥וּ עָלֶ֖יהָ דָּיֵ֥ק סָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: And it was in [the] year the ninth of his reigning, in the month the tenth, on [the] tenth of the month, came Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, he and all his army, against Jerusalem, and encamped against it, and they built against it siege-work all around.
pieces: On the tenth day of the tenth month, in the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon advanced on Jerusalem with his whole army. He camped against the city, and they built siege works against it on every side.

L.1: And it came about in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth [day] of the month, [that] Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came, he and all his army, against Jerusalem, and he encamped against it; and they built a siege wall against it all around.

R.1: In the ninth year that Zedekiah was king, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, marched against Jerusalem with his whole army. He set up camp around the city, and his soldiers built ramps and walls against it on every side.

decisions.choice: his reign: the reign of Zedekiah
decisions.reason: The last king named is Zedekiah, whom Nebuchadnezzar had set on the throne and who then rebelled against him (24:17-20). The siege is dated by the years of his reign.

decisions.choice: the tenth day of the tenth month of Zedekiah's ninth year: early in 588 BC
decisions.reason: Months are counted from the spring, so the tenth month falls in midwinter. Depending on how the reign years were counted, the siege began early in 588 BC or a year earlier. Ezekiel, among the exiles in Babylon, was told to write down this same day as the day the king of Babylon laid siege to Jerusalem (Ezekiel 24:1-2), and it was later kept as a fast day, "the fast of the tenth month" (Zechariah 8:19).

decisions.choice: siege works: a wall, ramps or towers built around a besieged city
decisions.reason: The word is used only of siege works (Ezekiel 4:2; 17:17; 21:27). It may mean a continuous wall that shut the city in, or the ramps and towers built against its walls; either way, the city was cut off.

decisions.choice: the fall of Jerusalem told again in Jeremiah 52 and 39
decisions.reason: Verses 1-21 and 27-30 of this chapter are repeated almost word for word in Jeremiah 52:4-34, and verses 1-12 are told again more briefly in Jeremiah 39:1-10. This verse matches Jeremiah 52:4; Jeremiah 39:1 gives only the year and month. Jeremiah 52 and 39 have not yet been drafted in this translation, so this wording is drafted fresh; when they are, the shared Hebrew should share its wording.

decisions.choice: Zedekiah (Balanced and Readable); his soldiers (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Zedekiah for "his", since the last verse of the previous chapter is far behind a reader who starts here. Readable says who "they" were who built the siege works, and describes them as ramps and walls.

records.heading: The fall of Jerusalem

records.source: וַתָּבֹ֥א הָעִ֖יר בַּמָּצ֑וֹר עַ֚ד עַשְׁתֵּ֣י עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ צִדְקִיָּֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: And came the city into the siege until [the] eleventh year of the king Zedekiah.
pieces: The city was under siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.

L.2: And the city came into the siege until the eleventh year of King Zedekiah.

R.2: The city was surrounded and cut off until Zedekiah's eleventh year as king.

decisions.choice: came into the siege: was besieged
decisions.reason: The city "came into" a state of siege and stayed in it: no one could go in or out, and food could not be brought in.

decisions.choice: until the eleventh year: about a year and a half
decisions.reason: From the tenth month of the ninth year (verse 1) to the fourth month of the eleventh year (verse 3, with Jeremiah 39:2) is about eighteen months. The siege was broken off for a time when an Egyptian army came out (Jeremiah 37:5-11), but the Babylonians returned.

decisions.choice: the same words in Jeremiah 52:5
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:5 has the same sentence. Jeremiah 39:2 joins this verse to the next and gives the full date of the breach.

decisions.choice: surrounded and cut off (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains what a siege is instead of using the word.

records.source: בְּתִשְׁעָ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ וַיֶּחֱזַ֥ק הָרָעָ֖ב בָּעִ֑יר וְלֹא־הָ֥יָה לֶ֖חֶם לְעַ֥ם הָאָֽרֶץ׃
records.gloss: On [the] ninth of the month, and was severe the famine in the city, and there was no bread for [the] people of the land.
pieces: By the ninth day of the fourth month the city was gripped by famine, and the people of the land had no food.

L.3: On the ninth [day] of the [fourth] month the famine was severe in the city, and there was no bread for the people of the land.

R.3: By the ninth day of the fourth month, there was a terrible famine in the city. The people had nothing left to eat.

decisions.choice: the ninth day of the fourth month
alternatives: the ninth day of the month (no month named)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew here names the day but not the month: "on the ninth of the month". The parallel accounts give the full date, "in the fourth month, on the ninth of the month" (Jeremiah 39:2; 52:6), and the number seems to have dropped out of this verse. The fourth month falls in midsummer, in 586 BC or a year earlier. It too was later kept as a fast day (Zechariah 8:19).

decisions.choice: bread: food of any kind
decisions.reason: "Bread" often stands for food in general (Genesis 3:19; Amos 4:6). Jeremiah's account of the siege speaks of bread running out in the city (Jeremiah 37:21; 38:9), and Lamentations 4:4-10 describes the famine.

decisions.choice: the people of the land: the ordinary people shut up in the city
decisions.reason: Elsewhere "the people of the land" can name the landowning citizens of Judah (11:14; 21:24; verse 19). Here it seems to mean the whole common population, including the country people who had fled inside the walls.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah 52:6 names the month
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:6 begins "In the fourth month, on the ninth of the month"; otherwise the verse is the same. Jeremiah 39:2 gives only the date, without the famine.

decisions.choice: [fourth] (Literal); fourth (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: The month is supplied from the parallel passages, in brackets at Literal, so that the date is complete.

records.source: וַתִּבָּקַ֣ע הָעִ֗יר וְכָל־אַנְשֵׁ֨י הַמִּלְחָמָ֤ה׀הַלַּ֨יְלָה֙ דֶּ֜רֶךְ שַׁ֣עַר׀בֵּ֣ין הַחֹמֹתַ֗יִם אֲשֶׁר֙ עַל־גַּ֣ן הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְכַשְׂדִּ֥ים עַל־הָעִ֖יר סָבִ֑יב וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ דֶּ֥רֶךְ הָעֲרָבָֽה׃
records.gloss: And was broken into the city, and all [the] men of the war [went] by night [by the] way of [the] gate between the two walls which [was] by [the] garden of the king, and [the] Chaldeans [were] against the city all around; and he went [the] way of the Arabah.
pieces: Then the city wall was breached, and all the soldiers fled by night through the gate between the two walls near the king's garden, though the Chaldeans were all around the city. The king went off toward the Arabah.

L.4: And the city was broken into, and all the men of war [fled] by night by way of the gate between the two walls, which [was] by the king's garden, while the Chaldeans [were] against the city all around; and he went by way of the Arabah.

R.4: Then the enemy broke through the city wall. That night all the soldiers escaped through the gate between the two walls near the king's garden, even though the Babylonians were all around the city. King Zedekiah fled toward the Jordan Valley.

decisions.choice: all the men of war fled by night
alternatives: the verb dropped from the text
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no verb for the soldiers: "all the men of war ... by night by way of the gate". The parallel accounts have "fled and went out of the city by night" (Jeremiah 52:7; compare 39:4), and the sense is clear from what follows.

decisions.choice: the gate between the two walls by the king's garden: at the south end of the city
decisions.reason: The king's garden lay at the south end of Jerusalem near the Pool of Siloam (Nehemiah 3:15). A gate there between two lines of wall led down into the valley, away from the main Babylonian lines.

decisions.choice: the Chaldeans: the Babylonians
decisions.reason: The Chaldeans were a people of southern Mesopotamia. Nebuchadnezzar's family was Chaldean, so the name came to mean the Babylonians and their army.

decisions.choice: he went: the king, Zedekiah
decisions.reason: The subject is not named, but verse 5 shows it is the king. The Arabah is the deep valley of the Jordan running down to the Dead Sea; Zedekiah was making for the river crossings near Jericho, perhaps to reach Ammon on the far side.

decisions.choice: told again in Jeremiah 52:7 and 39:4
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:7 adds that the soldiers "fled and went out of the city" and says "they went" toward the Arabah. Jeremiah 39:4 says that Zedekiah and the soldiers saw the Babylonian officers in the gate and fled.

decisions.choice: [fled] (Literal); fled, escaped (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: A verb is supplied for the soldiers, in brackets at Literal.

decisions.choice: the Babylonians; King Zedekiah; the Jordan Valley (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable uses the better-known name "Babylonians" for the Chaldeans throughout this chapter, names the king, and explains the Arabah as the Jordan Valley. Balanced says "the king" for "he".

records.source: וַיִּרְדְּפ֤וּ חֵיל־כַּשְׂדִּים֙ אַחַ֣ר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיַּשִּׂ֥גוּ אֹת֖וֹ בְּעַרְב֣וֹת יְרֵח֑וֹ וְכָל־חֵיל֔וֹ נָפֹ֖צוּ מֵעָלָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And pursued [the] army of [the] Chaldeans after the king, and overtook him in [the] plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him.
pieces: But the Chaldean army chased the king and caught up with him in the plains of Jericho, and his whole army scattered away from him.

L.5: And the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king, and they overtook him in the plains of Jericho; and all his army was scattered from him.

R.5: But the Babylonian army chased after the king and caught up with him on the plains near Jericho. All his soldiers scattered and left him.

decisions.choice: the plains of Jericho: the flat valley floor near the Jordan
decisions.reason: Jericho lies in the Jordan Valley some fifteen miles east of Jerusalem and far below it. Zedekiah had almost reached the river.

decisions.choice: his army was scattered from him: they ran off and left him alone
decisions.reason: The soldiers who had fled with him scattered, so the king was taken with no one to defend him. The Hebrew does not say whether they left him before the Babylonians reached him or when they arrived.

decisions.choice: told again in Jeremiah 52:8 and 39:5
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:8 has the same sentence; Jeremiah 39:5 joins it to the next verse.

decisions.choice: Babylonian (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 4.

records.source: וַֽיִּתְפְּשׂוּ֙ אֶת־הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיַּעֲל֥וּ אֹת֛וֹ אֶל־מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל רִבְלָ֑תָה וַיְדַבְּר֥וּ אִתּ֖וֹ מִשְׁפָּֽט׃
records.gloss: And they seized the king, and brought him up to [the] king of Babylon to Riblah, and they spoke with him judgment.
pieces: They seized the king and took him up to Riblah, to the king of Babylon, and there they passed sentence on him.

L.6: And they seized the king and brought him up to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and they spoke judgment with him.

R.6: They captured King Zedekiah and took him to the king of Babylon at the town of Riblah. There he was put on trial and sentenced.

decisions.choice: Riblah: a town far to the north, in Syria
decisions.reason: Riblah stood on the Orontes River in the land of Hamath (verse 21). Nebuchadnezzar directed his campaign from there, as Pharaoh Neco had held King Jehoahaz there (23:33).

decisions.choice: spoke judgment with him: tried him and passed sentence
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of bringing a legal case against someone (Jeremiah 1:16; 4:12). Zedekiah was judged as a vassal who had broken the oath of loyalty he had sworn to Nebuchadnezzar in God's name (24:20; 2 Chronicles 36:13; Ezekiel 17:13-20).

decisions.choice: Jeremiah: "he spoke judgment with him"
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:9 and 39:5 have the singular, "he" (the king of Babylon) passed sentence, and add that Riblah is "in the land of Hamath". Here the verb is plural, "they".

decisions.choice: put on trial and sentenced (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable spells out the legal sense of the idiom and names the king.

records.source: וְאֶת־בְּנֵי֙ צִדְקִיָּ֔הוּ שָׁחֲט֖וּ לְעֵינָ֑יו וְאֶת־עֵינֵ֤י צִדְקִיָּ֨הוּ֙ עִוֵּ֔ר וַיַּאַסְרֵ֨הוּ֙ בַֽנְחֻשְׁתַּ֔יִם וַיְבִאֵ֖הוּ בָּבֶֽל׃ס
records.gloss: And [the] sons of Zedekiah they slaughtered before his eyes; and [the] eyes of Zedekiah he blinded, and bound him with bronze fetters, and brought him [to] Babylon.
pieces: They slaughtered Zedekiah's sons while he watched. Then the king of Babylon put out Zedekiah's eyes, bound him in bronze fetters and took him to Babylon.

L.7: And they slaughtered the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes; and he put out the eyes of Zedekiah and bound him in bronze fetters and brought him [to] Babylon.

R.7: They killed Zedekiah's sons while he watched. Then the king of Babylon had Zedekiah's eyes put out. He had him bound in bronze chains and taken to Babylon.

decisions.choice: he put out his eyes: the king of Babylon
decisions.reason: The sons are killed by "they", but the blinding, binding and taking away are done by "he". The parallel passages name him: the king of Babylon (Jeremiah 52:10-11; 39:6-7).

decisions.choice: the sons killed, then the eyes put out
decisions.reason: Killing a rebel king's sons ended his line, and blinding was a punishment for rebel rulers in the ancient Near East; the last thing Zedekiah saw was the death of his sons.

decisions.choice: the prophets' words come true
decisions.reason: Jeremiah had told Zedekiah that he would see the king of Babylon face to face and be taken to Babylon (Jeremiah 32:4-5; 34:3), and Ezekiel had said that the prince would be brought to Babylon "but he will not see it, and there he will die" (Ezekiel 12:13). Both came true.

decisions.choice: bronze fetters: a pair of bronze shackles
decisions.reason: The word is "bronze" in the dual form, meaning a pair of bronze shackles, the same word used of Samson's fetters (Judges 16:21).

decisions.choice: told again in Jeremiah 52:10-11 and 39:6-7
decisions.reason: Jeremiah adds that the king of Babylon also killed the officials of Judah at Riblah, and Jeremiah 52:11 adds that Zedekiah was kept in prison until the day of his death.

decisions.choice: the king of Babylon (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the one Hebrew calls "he", from the parallel passages. Readable says he "had" these things done.

records.source: וּבַחֹ֤דֶשׁ הַֽחֲמִישִׁי֙ בְּשִׁבְעָ֣ה לַחֹ֔דֶשׁ הִ֗יא שְׁנַת֙ תְּשַֽׁע־עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לַמֶּ֖לֶךְ נְבֻכַדְנֶאצַּ֣ר מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֑ל בָּ֞א נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֧ן רַב־טַבָּחִ֛ים עֶ֥בֶד מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶ֖ל יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃
records.gloss: And in the month the fifth, on [the] seventh of the month, it [was the] year nineteen year of the king Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, came Nebuzaradan chief of [the] guards, servant of [the] king of Babylon, [to] Jerusalem.
pieces: In the fifth month, on the seventh day, the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar's reign over Babylon, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard, an official of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem.

L.8: And in the fifth month, on the seventh [day] of the month, which [was] the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard, a servant of the king of Babylon, came [to] Jerusalem.

R.8: On the seventh day of the fifth month, Nebuzaradan came to Jerusalem. He was the commander of the royal guard and an official of the king of Babylon. This was in the nineteenth year that Nebuchadnezzar was king of Babylon.

decisions.choice: chief of the guard: literally "chief of the slaughterers"
decisions.reason: The word for the guards first meant butchers or cooks, but in a royal title it names the king's bodyguard, who also carried out executions, as with Potiphar "commander of the guard" (Genesis 37:36). Here it is the title of a senior Babylonian officer. A Babylonian list of Nebuchadnezzar's court officials includes a Nabu-zer-iddin, which is the Babylonian form of the name Nebuzaradan, "the god Nabu has given offspring".

decisions.choice: the fifth month of Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year: midsummer 586 BC
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar's nineteenth year is Zedekiah's eleventh (verse 2). The burning of the temple came about a month after the city fell, and "the fast of the fifth month" was later kept in mourning for it (Zechariah 7:3, 5; 8:19).

decisions.choice: Jeremiah 52:12: the tenth day, and "who stood before the king of Babylon"
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:12 dates Nebuzaradan's arrival to the tenth of the month, not the seventh, and calls him one "who stood before the king of Babylon", a court officer, instead of "servant". The two dates may count his setting out and his arrival, or one number may have been miscopied. Jeremiah 39:9 gives no date.

decisions.choice: servant (Literal); official (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: As elsewhere for a king's servant who held office, Literal keeps "servant" and Balanced and Readable say "official".

decisions.choice: chief of the guard (Literal); captain of the guard (Balanced); commander of the royal guard (Readable)
decisions.reason: Each level uses its own wording for the title throughout this chapter. Readable moves the date by the king's reign to the end so that the sentence about Nebuzaradan stays short.

records.heading: The temple is burned

records.source: וַיִּשְׂרֹ֥ף אֶת־בֵּית־יְהוָ֖ה וְאֶת־בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־בָּתֵּ֧י יְרוּשָׁלִַ֛ם וְאֶת־כָּל־בֵּ֥ית גָּד֖וֹל שָׂרַ֥ף בָּאֵֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: And he burned [the] house of Yahweh and [the] house of the king, and all [the] houses of Jerusalem; and every house of [a] great [one] he burned with fire.
pieces: He burned the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the king's palace and all the houses of Jerusalem; every important house he burned down.

L.9: And he burned the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and the house of the king and all the houses of Jerusalem; and every great house he burned with fire.

R.9: He set fire to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple, the royal palace and all the houses in Jerusalem. He burned down every important building.

decisions.choice: the house of the LORD burned
decisions.reason: Solomon's temple (1 Kings 6-8) had stood for nearly four hundred years. The LORD had warned that if Israel turned away, the house he had set apart for his name would become a ruin (1 Kings 9:7-9), and had said of Jerusalem, "I will reject this city ... and the house of which I said, My name will be there" (23:27).

decisions.choice: every great house: the houses of the important people
decisions.reason: The Hebrew can mean every large building or the house of every "great one", the leading men of the city. Either way it points to the main buildings of Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: all the houses of Jerusalem; and every great house
alternatives: all the houses of Jerusalem, that is, every great house
decisions.reason: The last clause may simply add the great houses to the list, or it may explain the one before it: "all the houses of Jerusalem, that is, every great house", meaning the important buildings rather than every home.

decisions.choice: told again in Jeremiah 52:13 and 39:8
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:13 has the same sentence. Jeremiah 39:8 does not name the temple; it says the Chaldeans burned the king's house and "the house of the people".

decisions.choice: the king's palace; temple (Readable)
decisions.reason: "The house of the king" is the palace at Balanced and Readable. Readable says "temple" for the house of the LORD.

records.source: וְאֶת־חוֹמֹ֥ת יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סָבִ֑יב נָֽתְצוּ֙ כָּל־חֵ֣יל כַּשְׂדִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר רַב־טַבָּחִֽים׃
records.gloss: And [the] walls of Jerusalem all around broke down all [the] army of [the] Chaldeans who [were with the] chief of [the] guards.
pieces: The whole Chaldean army that was with the captain of the guard tore down the walls all around Jerusalem.

L.10: And all the army of the Chaldeans who [were with] the chief of the guard broke down the walls around Jerusalem.

R.10: The whole Babylonian army that was with the commander of the guard tore down the walls all around Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: who were with the chief of the guard
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "who ... the chief of the guard", without "with". Jeremiah 52:14 has "who were with the chief of the guard", which is the sense here.

decisions.choice: the walls broken down: the city left without defense
decisions.reason: Without walls a city could not protect itself or be counted a city at all. Jerusalem's walls lay in ruins until Nehemiah rebuilt them (Nehemiah 1:3; 2:17).

decisions.choice: told again in Jeremiah 52:14 and 39:8
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:14 has the same sentence with "with"; Jeremiah 39:8 says simply that the Chaldeans broke down the walls.

decisions.choice: [were with] (Literal); was with (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The missing words are supplied from the parallel, in brackets at Literal.

records.source: וְאֵת֩ יֶ֨תֶר הָעָ֜ם הַנִּשְׁאָרִ֣ים בָּעִ֗יר וְאֶת־הַנֹּֽפְלִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֤ר נָפְלוּ֙ עַל־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֔ל וְאֵ֖ת יֶ֣תֶר הֶהָמ֑וֹן הֶגְלָ֕ה נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֖ן רַב־טַבָּחִֽים׃
records.gloss: And [the] rest of the people who were left in the city, and the deserters who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and [the] rest of the multitude, exiled Nebuzaradan chief of [the] guards.
pieces: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried into exile the rest of the people who were left in the city, those who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the population.

L.11: And the rest of the people who were left in the city, and the deserters who had deserted to the king of Babylon, and the rest of the multitude, Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard carried into exile.

R.11: Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, took the rest of the people away as captives. These included the people still left in the city, those who had gone over to the side of the king of Babylon, and everyone else.

decisions.choice: fell to the king of Babylon: deserted to him
decisions.reason: To "fall to" an enemy means to go over to his side. Jeremiah had urged the people to do this to save their lives (Jeremiah 21:9; 38:2), and Zedekiah feared those who had done so (Jeremiah 38:19).

decisions.choice: the multitude: the rest of the population
decisions.reason: The word means a crowd or throng. Jeremiah 52:15 has a word that differs by one letter and means "craftsmen" or "master workers"; Jeremiah 39:9 repeats "the rest of the people who remained" instead.

decisions.choice: carried into exile: the second great deportation
decisions.reason: Eleven years earlier Nebuchadnezzar had taken King Jehoiachin, the leading men and the craftsmen to Babylon (24:14-16). Now the rest of the city's people went the same way.

decisions.choice: told again in Jeremiah 52:15 and 39:9
decisions.reason: Besides the word noted above, Jeremiah 52:15 begins the list with "some of the poorest of the people".

decisions.choice: Nebuzaradan ... carried into exile (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew puts the three groups first and the verb and its subject last. Literal keeps that order; Balanced and Readable start with Nebuzaradan, and Readable lists the groups in a second sentence.

records.source: וּמִדַּלַּ֣ת הָאָ֔רֶץ הִשְׁאִ֖יר רַב־טַבָּחִ֑ים לְכֹֽרְמִ֖ים וּלְיֹגְבִֽים׃
records.gloss: And some of [the] poor of the land left [the] chief of [the] guards for vinedressers and for field-workers.
pieces: But the captain of the guard left some of the poorest people of the land to tend the vineyards and work the fields.

L.12: But some of the poorest of the land the chief of the guard left as vinedressers and as field workers.

R.12: But the commander of the guard left behind some of the poorest people in the land. He had them take care of the vineyards and work the fields.

decisions.choice: field workers: probably plowmen or farm laborers
decisions.reason: The word appears only here and in Jeremiah 52:16, and its exact sense is not known. The setting beside "vinedressers" shows it names some kind of work on the land, perhaps plowing or tilling.

decisions.choice: some of the poorest left to work the land
decisions.reason: The land was not left empty. Those who had owned nothing were left to keep the vineyards and fields producing, and Jeremiah 39:10 says they were given vineyards and fields. When Jehoiachin was taken, likewise, "no one remained except the poorest people of the land" (24:14).

decisions.choice: told again in Jeremiah 52:16 and 39:10
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:16 has the same sentence; Jeremiah 39:10 adds that Nebuzaradan gave the poor vineyards and fields on that day.

decisions.choice: to tend the vineyards and work the fields (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the work instead of using the nouns "vinedressers" and "field workers".

records.source: וְאֶת־עַמּוּדֵ֨י הַנְּחֹ֜שֶׁת אֲשֶׁ֣ר בֵּית־יְהוָ֗ה וְֽאֶת־הַמְּכֹנ֞וֹת וְאֶת־יָ֧ם הַנְּחֹ֛שֶׁת אֲשֶׁ֥ר בְּבֵית־יְהוָ֖ה שִׁבְּר֣וּ כַשְׂדִּ֑ים וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ אֶת־נְחֻשְׁתָּ֖ם בָּבֶֽלָה׃
records.gloss: And [the] pillars of the bronze which [were in the] house of Yahweh, and the stands, and [the] sea of the bronze which [was] in [the] house of Yahweh, broke in pieces [the] Chaldeans, and carried their bronze to Babylon.
pieces: The Chaldeans broke up the bronze pillars that were in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the stands, and the bronze Sea that was in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and they hauled the metal off to Babylon.

L.13: And the pillars of bronze that [were in] the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and the stands and the sea of bronze that [was] in the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the Chaldeans broke in pieces, and they carried their bronze to Babylon.

R.13: The Babylonians broke into pieces the bronze pillars in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple, the bronze stands on wheels, and the huge bronze tank called the Sea. They carried all the bronze away to Babylon.

decisions.choice: the pillars, the stands and the Sea that Solomon had made
decisions.reason: These are the great bronze works cast for Solomon's temple: the two pillars at the porch (1 Kings 7:15-22), the great basin called the Sea (1 Kings 7:23-26), and the ten wheeled stands for basins of water (1 Kings 7:27-37). The pillars were named Jachin and Boaz (1 Kings 7:21), but they are not named here.

decisions.choice: broken in pieces and the bronze carried off
decisions.reason: The pieces were too large to carry whole, so they were broken up and taken for their metal. Jeremiah had warned that the pillars, the Sea and the stands still left in the temple would be carried to Babylon (Jeremiah 27:19-22).

decisions.choice: the same words in Jeremiah 52:17
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:17 has the same sentence.

decisions.choice: the Sea; stands on wheels, a huge bronze tank called the Sea (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 7:23 and 27, Balanced writes "the Sea" as a name, and Readable says what the stands and the Sea were. Readable says "temple" for the house of the LORD and mentions it once.

records.source: וְאֶת־הַסִּירֹ֨ת וְאֶת־הַיָּעִ֜ים וְאֶת־הַֽמְזַמְּר֣וֹת וְאֶת־הַכַּפּ֗וֹת וְאֵ֨ת כָּל־כְּלֵ֧י הַנְּחֹ֛שֶׁת אֲשֶׁ֥ר יְשָֽׁרְתוּ־בָ֖ם לָקָֽחוּ׃
records.gloss: And the pots and the shovels and the snuffers and the dishes and all [the] vessels of the bronze which they served with them, they took.
pieces: They also took away the pots, the shovels, the wick trimmers, the dishes and all the bronze utensils used in the temple service.

L.14: And the pots and the shovels and the snuffers and the dishes and all the vessels of bronze with which they served, they took away.

R.14: They also took the pots, shovels, wick trimmers and dishes, and all the other bronze things used in the worship at the temple.

decisions.choice: pots, shovels, snuffers, dishes: tools for the altar, the lamps and the incense
decisions.reason: The pots carried away ashes and the shovels served the altar (1 Kings 7:40, 45); the snuffers trimmed the lamp wicks (1 Kings 7:50); the dishes held incense (Numbers 7:14).

decisions.choice: served: the priests' ministry in the temple
decisions.reason: The verb is used of the priests' service at the altar and in the sanctuary (Exodus 28:43; Numbers 4:12).

decisions.choice: Jeremiah 52:18 adds the basins
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:18 has the same list with "the basins" added after the snuffers.

decisions.choice: snuffers (Literal); wick trimmers (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 7:50.

decisions.choice: in the temple service, in the worship at the temple (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: "They served with them" is the priests' service in the temple; Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: וְאֶת־הַמַּחְתּוֹת֙ וְאֶת־הַמִּזְרָק֗וֹת אֲשֶׁ֤ר זָהָב֙ זָהָ֔ב וַאֲשֶׁר־כֶּ֖סֶף כָּ֑סֶף לָקַ֖ח רַב־טַבָּחִֽים׃
records.gloss: And the firepans and the bowls, which [were] gold [as] gold, and which [were] silver [as] silver, took [the] chief of [the] guards.
pieces: The captain of the guard took away the firepans and the sprinkling bowls, everything that was made of gold and everything that was made of silver.

L.15: And the firepans and the bowls, what [was] gold, gold, and what [was] silver, silver, the chief of the guard took away.

R.15: The commander of the guard also took the fire pans and the sprinkling bowls. He took everything made of gold and everything made of silver.

decisions.choice: gold, gold; silver, silver: everything of gold and everything of silver
alternatives: of pure gold and pure silver
taken for their gold and silver
decisions.reason: The doubled word gathers everything of that metal: whatever was gold and whatever was silver. Some take it to stress the metal, "pure gold" or "for their gold", that is, taken for the value of the metal.

decisions.choice: the last of the temple's treasures
decisions.reason: Nebuchadnezzar had already cut up the gold vessels Solomon made when he took Jehoiachin (24:13). Later the temple vessels in Babylon were used at Belshazzar's feast (Daniel 5:2-3) and given back by Cyrus (Ezra 1:7-11).

decisions.choice: Jeremiah 52:19 lists more
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:19 has a longer list of what the captain of the guard took: basins, firepans, bowls, pots, lampstands, dishes and cups.

decisions.choice: firepans; bowls (Literal), sprinkling bowls (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 7:40 and 50; Readable writes "fire pans".

records.source: הָעַמּוּדִ֣ים׀שְׁנַ֗יִם הַיָּ֤ם הָֽאֶחָד֙ וְהַמְּכֹנ֔וֹת אֲשֶׁר־עָשָׂ֥ה שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְבֵ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה לֹא־הָיָ֣ה מִשְׁקָ֔ל לִנְחֹ֖שֶׁת כָּל־הַכֵּלִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: The pillars two, the sea the one, and the stands which made Solomon for [the] house of Yahweh, there was no weight to [the] bronze of all the vessels these.
pieces: As for the two pillars, the one Sea and the stands Solomon made for the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the bronze of all these things was more than could be weighed.

L.16: The two pillars, the one sea, and the stands that Solomon had made for the house of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: there was no weight for the bronze of all these vessels.

R.16: The two pillars, the Sea and the stands that King Solomon had made for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple held so much bronze that no one could weigh it.

decisions.choice: there was no weight: it was too much to weigh
decisions.reason: The words repeat 1 Kings 7:47, where Solomon left the bronze unweighed because there was so much of it. What was too great to weigh when the temple was built is now carried away.

decisions.choice: the list stands first, then what is said about it
decisions.reason: The verse names the great pieces again and then comments on them, a way of summing up verses 13-15.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah 52:20 adds the twelve bronze oxen
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:20 adds "the twelve bronze oxen that were under" the Sea. Kings says that King Ahaz had taken the Sea down from the oxen and set it on a stone base (16:17), which may be why the oxen are not named here.

decisions.choice: the Sea; King Solomon (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable leaves out "one" with the Sea and adds Solomon's title.

records.source: שְׁמֹנֶה֩ עֶשְׂרֵ֨ה אַמָּ֜ה קוֹמַ֣ת׀הָעַמּ֣וּד הָאֶחָ֗ד וְכֹתֶ֨רֶת עָלָ֥יו׀נְחֹשֶׁת֮ וְקוֹמַ֣ת הַכֹּתֶרֶת֮ שָׁלֹ֣שׁ אַמּוֹת֒ וּשְׂבָכָ֨ה וְרִמֹּנִ֧ים עַֽל־הַכֹּתֶ֛רֶת סָבִ֖יב הַכֹּ֣ל נְחֹ֑שֶׁת וְכָאֵ֛לֶּה לַֽעַמּ֥וּד הַשֵּׁנִ֖י עַל־הַשְּׂבָכָֽה׃
records.gloss: Eighteen cubit[s] [was the] height of the pillar the one, and a capital on it [of] bronze, and [the] height of the capital three cubits, and a network and pomegranates on the capital all around, the whole [of] bronze; and like these [was] to the pillar the second, with the network.
pieces: One pillar was {{units:about 27 feet|eighteen cubits}} high, with a bronze capital on top of it. The capital was {{units:about 4 1/2 feet|three cubits}} high, with a network and pomegranates all around it, all of bronze. The second pillar, with its network, was the same.

L.17: Eighteen cubits [was] the height of the one pillar, and on it [was] a capital of bronze; and the height of the capital [was] three cubits, and a network and pomegranates [were] on the capital all around, all of bronze; and the second pillar [had] the like, with the network.

R.17: The first pillar was {{units:about 27 feet|eighteen cubits}} tall. It had a bronze top, called a capital, that was {{units:about 4 1/2 feet|three cubits}} tall. All around the capital was a net of lattice work with pomegranates on it, all made of bronze. The second pillar was just the same.

decisions.choice: three cubits: the capital's height here; five in 1 Kings 7:16
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 7:16, Jeremiah 52:22 and 2 Chronicles 3:15 all give the capitals a height of five cubits. The three here may be a copying error, or it may measure only part of the capital, leaving out the lily work at its top (1 Kings 7:19). The Hebrew of this verse is followed.

decisions.choice: network and pomegranates: a lattice with bronze fruit
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 7:17-20, the network is a lattice of crossing bands around the capital, and the pomegranates are bronze ornaments in rows on it.

decisions.choice: the pillars described in 1 Kings 7:15-22 and Jeremiah 52:21-23
decisions.reason: The height of eighteen cubits matches 1 Kings 7:15. Jeremiah 52:21-23 adds the measure around each pillar (twelve cubits), that they were hollow, the thickness of the metal (four fingers), and the number of pomegranates (ninety-six on the sides, a hundred in all).

decisions.choice: like these to the second pillar: the second was the same
decisions.reason: Everything said of the first pillar holds for the second, "with the network" naming the part just described.

decisions.choice: a bronze top, called a capital (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in 1 Kings 7:16, Readable explains "capital" the first time.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֣ח רַב־טַבָּחִ֗ים אֶת־שְׂרָיָה֙ כֹּהֵ֣ן הָרֹ֔אשׁ וְאֶת־צְפַנְיָ֖הוּ כֹּהֵ֣ן מִשְׁנֶ֑ה וְאֶת־שְׁלֹ֖שֶׁת שֹׁמְרֵ֥י הַסַּֽף׃
records.gloss: And took [the] chief of [the] guards Seraiah [the] priest of the head, and Zephaniah [the] priest of second [rank], and [the] three keepers of the threshold.
pieces: The captain of the guard also seized Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the priest next to him, and the three doorkeepers.

L.18: And the chief of the guard took Seraiah the head priest and Zephaniah the second priest and the three keepers of the threshold.

R.18: The commander of the guard also arrested Seraiah the high priest, Zephaniah the priest next in rank, and the three men who guarded the temple entrance.

decisions.choice: Seraiah the head priest: the high priest
decisions.reason: "The head priest" is the leading priest of the temple (2 Chronicles 19:11; 26:20). Seraiah was the grandson of Hilkiah, the high priest under Josiah (22:4), and an ancestor of Ezra (1 Chronicles 5:39-40; Ezra 7:1). His son Jehozadak was taken into exile (1 Chronicles 5:41).

decisions.choice: Zephaniah the second priest: the high priest's deputy
decisions.reason: The priest "of second rank" was next after the high priest (23:4). Zephaniah son of Maaseiah carried messages between King Zedekiah and Jeremiah (Jeremiah 21:1; 29:25-29; 37:3).

decisions.choice: the keepers of the threshold: senior temple officers
decisions.reason: They guarded the entrances of the temple and received the money brought in (12:10; 22:4). The three were probably the heads of the gatekeepers.

decisions.choice: the same words in Jeremiah 52:24
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:24 has the same sentence.

decisions.choice: arrested; the high priest; the men who guarded the temple entrance (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "took" means here and explains the titles. Balanced says "doorkeepers".

records.source: וּמִן־הָעִ֡יר לָקַח֩ סָרִ֨יס אֶחָ֜ד אֲֽשֶׁר־ה֥וּא פָקִ֣יד׀עַל־אַנְשֵׁ֣י הַמִּלְחָמָ֗ה וַחֲמִשָּׁ֨ה אֲנָשִׁ֜ים מֵרֹאֵ֤י פְנֵֽי־הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר נִמְצְא֣וּ בָעִ֔יר וְאֵ֗ת הַסֹּפֵר֙ שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֔א הַמַּצְבִּ֖א אֶת־עַ֣ם הָאָ֑רֶץ וְשִׁשִּׁ֥ים אִישׁ֙ מֵעַ֣ם הָאָ֔רֶץ הַֽנִּמְצְאִ֖ים בָּעִֽיר׃
records.gloss: And from the city he took one official who he [was] appointed over [the] men of the war, and five men of [those] seeing [the] face of the king who were found in the city, and the scribe [of the] commander of the army, the one mustering the people of the land, and sixty men of [the] people of the land, the ones found in the city.
pieces: From the city he took an official who had been in charge of the soldiers, five of the king's advisers who were found in the city, the secretary of the commander of the army, who mustered the people of the land for war, and sixty of the people of the land who were still in the city.

L.19: And from the city he took one eunuch who [was] the overseer over the men of war, and five men of those who saw the face of the king, who were found in the city, and the scribe of the commander of the army, who mustered the people of the land, and sixty men of the people of the land who were found in the city.

R.19: From the city he also took the officer in charge of the soldiers and five of the king's close advisers who were still in the city. He took the army commander's secretary, who called up the men of the land to serve in the army. He also took sixty of those men who were still in the city.

decisions.choice: official: a royal officer
decisions.reason: The word can mean a eunuch, but it was also a general title for a high officer of the king (Genesis 37:36). Here it is a military officer in command of the soldiers.

decisions.choice: those who saw the face of the king: his closest advisers
decisions.reason: Only trusted counselors were allowed into the king's presence (Esther 1:14). Jeremiah 52:25 says there were seven of them, not five.

decisions.choice: the scribe of the commander of the army
alternatives: the scribe, who was commander of the army
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "the scribe, the commander of the army", which could mean that the secretary also commanded the army. Jeremiah 52:25 reads "the scribe of the commander of the army", and the next words, "who mustered the people of the land", fit a secretary who kept the lists for calling men up.

decisions.choice: the people of the land: the landholding men of Judah
decisions.reason: Here the phrase names the citizens of Judah who held land and were called up to fight (11:14; 21:24; 23:30). The sixty were probably leading men of that class.

decisions.choice: told again in Jeremiah 52:25
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:25 has "seven men" for "five men" and "the scribe of the commander"; otherwise it is the same.

decisions.choice: the king's advisers; mustered ... for war (Balanced); called up ... to serve in the army (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "those who saw the king's face" were, and what mustering was for. Readable splits the list into three sentences and uses "army commander" for the title, as elsewhere in these books.

decisions.choice: eunuch (Literal); official (Balanced); officer (Readable)
decisions.reason: As set for these books, Literal keeps "eunuch" for this word and Balanced and Readable say what he was here, a royal officer (m1).

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֹתָ֔ם נְבוּזַרְאֲדָ֖ן רַב־טַבָּחִ֑ים וַיֹּ֧לֶךְ אֹתָ֛ם עַל־מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל רִבְלָֽתָה׃
records.gloss: And took them Nebuzaradan chief of [the] guards, and brought them to [the] king of Babylon to Riblah.
pieces: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard led them away to Riblah and brought them before the king of Babylon.

L.20: And Nebuzaradan the chief of the guard took them and brought them to the king of Babylon, to Riblah.

R.20: Nebuzaradan, the commander of the guard, took them all to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

decisions.choice: Riblah: Nebuchadnezzar's camp in Syria
decisions.reason: As in verse 6, where Zedekiah had been judged.

decisions.choice: the same words in Jeremiah 52:26
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:26 has the same sentence.

records.source: וַיַּ֣ךְ אֹתָם֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ בָּבֶ֧ל וַיְמִיתֵ֛ם בְּרִבְלָ֖ה בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חֲמָ֑ת וַיִּ֥גֶל יְהוּדָ֖ה מֵעַ֥ל אַדְמָתֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And struck them [the] king of Babylon and put them to death at Riblah in [the] land of Hamath. And went into exile Judah from upon its land.
pieces: The king of Babylon had them struck down and executed at Riblah, in the land of Hamath. So Judah went into exile, away from its own land.

L.21: And the king of Babylon struck them and put them to death at Riblah in the land of Hamath. So Judah went into exile from its land.

R.21: The king of Babylon had them killed there at Riblah, in the land of Hamath. So the people of Judah were taken away from their land as captives.

decisions.choice: the land of Hamath: the region of central Syria
decisions.reason: Hamath was a kingdom on the Orontes River, north of Israel; Riblah lay in its territory.

decisions.choice: Judah went into exile from its land
decisions.reason: The same words were said of the northern kingdom: "Israel went into exile from its land" (17:23). The LORD had warned that unfaithfulness would end in exile (Leviticus 26:33; Deuteronomy 28:36, 64), and had said that he would remove Judah from his sight as he had removed Israel (23:27).

decisions.choice: Jeremiah 52:27 is the same; then the accounts part
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:27 has the same sentence. Jeremiah then lists the numbers taken into exile in three deportations (Jeremiah 52:28-30), while Kings tells instead what became of those left in the land (verses 22-26).

decisions.choice: the people of Judah (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says "the people of Judah" for the nation, and "as captives" for going into exile.

records.source: וְהָעָ֗ם הַנִּשְׁאָר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר הִשְׁאִ֔יר נְבֽוּכַדְנֶאצַּ֖ר מֶ֣לֶךְ בָּבֶ֑ל וַיַּפְקֵ֣ד עֲלֵיהֶ֔ם אֶת־גְּדַלְיָ֖הוּ בֶּן־אֲחִיקָ֥ם בֶּן־שָׁפָֽן׃פ
records.gloss: And the people who remained in [the] land of Judah, whom left Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, and he appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan.
pieces: Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon made Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, governor over the people he had left in the land of Judah.

L.22: And [as for] the people who remained in the land of Judah, whom Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had left, he appointed over them Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan.

R.22: Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, put Gedaliah son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, in charge of the people he had left behind in the land of Judah.

decisions.choice: Gedaliah son of Ahikam son of Shaphan: from a leading family of officials
decisions.reason: Shaphan was King Josiah's secretary, and his son Ahikam was among those Josiah sent to inquire about the book of the law (22:3-14). Ahikam had protected Jeremiah when others wanted him put to death (Jeremiah 26:24). The family had supported Jeremiah's counsel to submit to Babylon.

decisions.choice: appointed over them: made him governor
decisions.reason: No title is given, but Gedaliah was set over the people left in Judah, answering to the king of Babylon (Jeremiah 40:5, 7).

decisions.choice: verses 22-26 sum up Jeremiah 40-43
decisions.reason: The story of Gedaliah, his murder and the flight to Egypt is told at length in Jeremiah 40:7-41:18 and 43:1-7. Kings gives a short summary.

decisions.choice: Nebuchadnezzar ... made Gedaliah ... governor over (Balanced); put Gedaliah in charge (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the people first and then says "he appointed over them". Balanced and Readable start with Nebuchadnezzar, the one who made the appointment; Balanced uses "governor" for the office (see the meaning decision above).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמְעוּ֩ כָל־שָׂרֵ֨י הַחֲיָלִ֜ים הֵ֣מָּה וְהָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים כִּֽי־הִפְקִ֤יד מֶֽלֶךְ־בָּבֶל֙ אֶת־גְּדַלְיָ֔הוּ וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ אֶל־גְּדַלְיָ֖הוּ הַמִּצְפָּ֑ה וְיִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בֶּן־נְתַנְיָ֡ה וְיוֹחָנָ֣ן בֶּן־קָ֠רֵחַ וּשְׂרָיָ֨ה בֶן־תַּנְחֻ֜מֶת הַנְּטֹפָתִ֗י וְיַֽאֲזַנְיָ֨הוּ֙ בֶּן־הַמַּ֣עֲכָתִ֔י הֵ֖מָּה וְאַנְשֵׁיהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And heard all [the] commanders of the forces, they and the men, that had appointed [the] king of Babylon Gedaliah, and they came to Gedaliah [to] Mizpah: and Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and Johanan son of Kareah, and Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, they and their men.
pieces: All the commanders of the forces and their men learned that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah, and they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah. They were Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, together with their men.

L.23: And all the commanders of the forces, they and the men, heard that the king of Babylon had appointed Gedaliah, and they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, and Johanan son of Kareah, and Seraiah son of Tanhumeth the Netophathite, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite, they and their men.

R.23: All the army commanders and their men heard that the king of Babylon had put Gedaliah in charge. So they came to Gedaliah at Mizpah. They were Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan son of Kareah, Seraiah son of Tanhumeth from the town of Netophah, and Jaazaniah son of the Maacathite. Their men came with them.

decisions.choice: the commanders of the forces: Judah's officers still at large
decisions.reason: These were officers of Judah's army who had not been captured and were still out in the countryside with their men (Jeremiah 40:7).

decisions.choice: Mizpah: a town of Benjamin north of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Mizpah lay a few miles north of Jerusalem and had long been a gathering place for Israel (1 Samuel 7:5-6; 10:17). With Jerusalem in ruins, Gedaliah governed from there.

decisions.choice: the Netophathite; the Maacathite
decisions.reason: Netophah was a town near Bethlehem (Ezra 2:22; 2 Samuel 23:28). The Maacathites were a clan named for Maacah, a small Aramean region northeast of Galilee (Deuteronomy 3:14; 2 Samuel 23:34); Jaazaniah's father is named only by his clan.

decisions.choice: a fuller list in Jeremiah 40:7-8
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 40:8 also names Jonathan son of Kareah and the sons of Ephai the Netophathite, and spells Jaazaniah as Jezaniah.

decisions.choice: from the town of Netophah (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains "the Netophathite" by naming his town.

records.heading: Gedaliah at Mizpah

records.source: וַיִּשָּׁבַ֨ע לָהֶ֤ם גְּדַלְיָ֨הוּ֙ וּלְאַנְשֵׁיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֔ם אַל־תִּֽירְא֖וּ מֵעַבְדֵ֣י הַכַּשְׂדִּ֑ים שְׁב֣וּ בָאָ֗רֶץ וְעִבְד֛וּ אֶת־מֶ֥לֶךְ בָּבֶ֖ל וְיִטַ֥ב לָכֶֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And swore to them Gedaliah and to their men, and said to them, Do not fear from [the] servants of the Chaldeans; dwell in the land and serve [the] king of Babylon, and it will be good for you.
pieces: Gedaliah swore an oath to them and their men. "Do not be afraid of the Chaldean officials," he said. "Settle in the land, serve the king of Babylon, and all will go well with you."

L.24: And Gedaliah swore to them and to their men, and he said to them, "Do not be afraid of the servants of the Chaldeans. Dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will be well with you."

R.24: Gedaliah gave them and their men his promise, and he swore an oath to keep it. "Do not be afraid of the Babylonian officials," he said. "Stay in the land and serve the king of Babylon. Then things will go well for you."

decisions.choice: swore to them: gave his word under oath
decisions.reason: Gedaliah guaranteed with an oath that the commanders and their men would be safe if they accepted Babylonian rule.

decisions.choice: the servants of the Chaldeans: the Babylonian officials
decisions.reason: The "servants" are the officers who governed for Babylon. Jeremiah 40:9 has instead "Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans".

decisions.choice: the counsel Jeremiah had given
decisions.reason: Gedaliah repeats the message Jeremiah had long given: serve the king of Babylon and live (Jeremiah 27:11-12; 38:17), settle where you are and seek its good (Jeremiah 29:4-7). Jeremiah 40:9-10 gives Gedaliah's words more fully.

decisions.choice: servants (Literal); officials (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 8.

decisions.choice: he said, placed inside the speech (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable put "he said" after the first sentence of the speech, so the oath and the words are not joined by a long run of "and". Readable says what the oath was for.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י׀בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י בָּ֣א יִשְׁמָעֵ֣אל בֶּן־נְ֠תַנְיָה בֶּן־אֱלִ֨ישָׁמָ֜ע מִזֶּ֣רַע הַמְּלוּכָ֗ה וַעֲשָׂרָ֤ה אֲנָשִׁים֙ אִתּ֔וֹ וַיַּכּ֥וּ אֶת־גְּדַלְיָ֖הוּ וַיָּמֹ֑ת וְאֶת־הַיְּהוּדִים֙ וְאֶת־הַכַּשְׂדִּ֔ים אֲשֶׁר־הָי֥וּ אִתּ֖וֹ בַּמִּצְפָּֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was in the month the seventh, came Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elishama, of [the] seed of the kingship, and ten men with him, and they struck Gedaliah and he died, and the Judeans and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.
pieces: But in the seventh month Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, who was of royal descent, came with ten men and struck down Gedaliah and killed him, together with the Judeans and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.

L.25: And it came about in the seventh month [that] Ishmael son of Nethaniah son of Elishama, of the royal seed, came, and ten men with him, and they struck Gedaliah, and he died, and the Judeans and the Chaldeans who were with him at Mizpah.

R.25: But in the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah and grandson of Elishama came to Mizpah with ten men. Ishmael was a member of the royal family. He and his men attacked and killed Gedaliah. They also killed the Judeans and the Babylonians who were with Gedaliah at Mizpah.

decisions.choice: the seventh month: autumn, probably of the same year
decisions.reason: No year is given here or in Jeremiah 41:1. It is usually taken to be the same year, two months after the temple was burned. Some think it was a later year, since Jeremiah 52:30 mentions another deportation five years later.

decisions.choice: of the royal seed: a member of the family of David
decisions.reason: Ishmael belonged to the royal line and may have resented a governor from outside it who served Babylon. Jeremiah 40:14 says that Baalis king of Ammon had sent him to kill Gedaliah.

decisions.choice: the murder later mourned with a fast
decisions.reason: "The fast of the seventh month" is named beside the fasts of the fourth, fifth and tenth months (Zechariah 7:5; 8:19), which match the dates in verses 1, 3 and 8. In Jewish tradition it is kept as the fast of Gedaliah.

decisions.choice: told at length in Jeremiah 41:1-3
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 41:1-3 adds that Ishmael and his men ate a meal with Gedaliah at Mizpah before killing him, and that the dead included the soldiers there.

decisions.choice: grandson of Elishama; They also killed (Readable); and killed him (Balanced)
decisions.reason: "Son of Nethaniah son of Elishama" names his father and grandfather, and Readable says so. Balanced and Readable spell out that the Judeans and the Chaldeans were killed too, which the Hebrew implies by joining them to "they struck".

records.source: וַיָּקֻ֨מוּ כָל־הָעָ֜ם מִקָּטֹ֤ן וְעַד־גָּדוֹל֙ וְשָׂרֵ֣י הַחֲיָלִ֔ים וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ מִצְרָ֑יִם כִּ֥י יָרְא֖וּ מִפְּנֵ֥י כַשְׂדִּֽים׃פ
records.gloss: And arose all the people, from small and to great, and [the] commanders of the forces, and they went [to] Egypt, for they were afraid from [the] face of [the] Chaldeans.
pieces: Then all the people, from the least to the greatest, and the commanders of the forces set out and went to Egypt, because they were afraid of the Chaldeans.

L.26: And all the people, from small to great, and the commanders of the forces arose and went [to] Egypt, because they were afraid of the Chaldeans.

R.26: Then all the people, from the least important to the most important, left with the army commanders and went to Egypt. They were afraid of what the Babylonians would do to them.

decisions.choice: from small to great: everyone, whatever their rank or age
decisions.reason: The pair takes in the whole people, from the least important to the most important (Jeremiah 6:13; 42:1).

decisions.choice: afraid of the face of the Chaldeans: afraid of what they would do
decisions.reason: They feared that Babylon would punish them all for the murder of its governor and its soldiers (Jeremiah 41:18).

decisions.choice: the flight to Egypt told in Jeremiah 42-43
decisions.reason: Jeremiah told them in the LORD's name to stay in the land and not go to Egypt (Jeremiah 42:9-19), but they went anyway and took him with them (Jeremiah 43:1-7). After the story of the exodus, the people's return to Egypt undoes their deliverance, as Deuteronomy 28:68 had warned.

decisions.choice: afraid of what the Babylonians would do to them (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom and joins the people to the commanders with "left with".

records.source: וַיְהִי֩ בִשְׁלֹשִׁ֨ים וָשֶׁ֜בַע שָׁנָ֗ה לְגָלוּת֙ יְהוֹיָכִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֔ה בִּשְׁנֵ֤ים עָשָׂר֙ חֹ֔דֶשׁ בְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְשִׁבְעָ֖ה לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ נָשָׂ֡א אֱוִ֣יל מְרֹדַךְ֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ בָּבֶ֜ל בִּשְׁנַ֣ת מָלְכ֗וֹ אֶת־רֹ֛אשׁ יְהוֹיָכִ֥ין מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָ֖ה מִבֵּ֥ית כֶּֽלֶא׃
records.gloss: And it was in [the] thirty and seven year of [the] exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in [the] twelfth month, on [the] twenty and seven of the month, lifted Evil-Merodach king of Babylon, in [the] year of his reigning, [the] head of Jehoiachin king of Judah from [the] house of imprisonment.
pieces: In the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month, Evil-Merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, showed favor to Jehoiachin king of Judah and released him from prison.

L.27: And it came about in the thirty-seventh year of the exile of Jehoiachin king of Judah, in the twelfth month, on the twenty-seventh [day] of the month, [that] Evil-Merodach king of Babylon, in the year he became king, lifted up the head of Jehoiachin king of Judah from the house of imprisonment.

R.27: Jehoiachin king of Judah had been in exile for thirty-seven years. Then Evil-Merodach became king of Babylon. In the year he became king, on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month, he showed Jehoiachin favor and let him out of prison.

decisions.choice: lifted up the head: showed favor and released
decisions.reason: To lift up someone's head is to raise him from disgrace to favor, as Pharaoh lifted up the head of his cupbearer and brought him out of prison (Genesis 40:13, 20). Here it goes with release "from the house of imprisonment".

decisions.choice: Evil-Merodach: the Babylonian king Awel-Marduk
decisions.reason: The name is the Hebrew form of Awel-Marduk, "man of Marduk", Nebuchadnezzar's son, who reigned for about two years. In Hebrew the first part sounds like the word for "foolish", which may be no more than the way the name was heard, or a scornful twist.

decisions.choice: the thirty-seventh year: about 561 BC
decisions.reason: Jehoiachin was taken to Babylon at eighteen, in 597 BC (24:8-15). Thirty-seven years later, in the year Evil-Merodach came to the throne, he was about fifty-five. The twelfth month falls at the end of winter.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah 52:31: the twenty-fifth day
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:31 has the same sentence but dates the release to the twenty-fifth of the month, not the twenty-seventh. The difference may come from copying, or from counting the order and the release separately.

decisions.choice: showed favor ... and released him (Balanced); showed Jehoiachin favor and let him out (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give both sides of the idiom with two verbs instead of keeping the picture of lifting the head. Readable splits the date into short sentences.

records.heading: Jehoiachin is released

records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ טֹב֑וֹת וַיִּתֵּן֙ אֶת־כִּסְא֔וֹ מֵעַ֗ל כִּסֵּ֧א הַמְּלָכִ֛ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר אִתּ֖וֹ בְּבָבֶֽל׃
records.gloss: And he spoke with him good things, and set his seat above [the] seat of the kings who [were] with him in Babylon.
pieces: He spoke kindly to him and gave him a seat of honor above the seats of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.

L.28: And he spoke good things with him and set his seat above the seat of the kings who [were] with him in Babylon.

R.28: He spoke kindly to Jehoiachin and gave him a place of honor, higher than that of the other kings who were with him in Babylon.

decisions.choice: spoke good things with him: spoke kindly to him
decisions.reason: To speak "good things" is to speak kindly and favorably (Jeremiah 12:6). It may also suggest that the king promised him good treatment, as a ruler gives terms to one he has taken under his protection.

decisions.choice: the seat above the other kings: first place among the captive kings
decisions.reason: The Babylonian kings kept rulers of conquered lands at their court. Jehoiachin was given a seat higher than all of them, a public sign of honor.

decisions.choice: who were with him: with Jehoiachin or with the king
decisions.reason: "Him" may be Jehoiachin, the kings who were held with him, or Evil-Merodach, the kings at his court. The sense is the same: the other kings in Babylon.

decisions.choice: the same words in Jeremiah 52:32
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:32 has the same sentence.

decisions.choice: a seat of honor; a place of honor (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what setting his seat above the others meant, and add "other" for the kings.

records.source: וְשִׁנָּ֕א אֵ֖ת בִּגְדֵ֣י כִלְא֑וֹ וְאָכַ֨ל לֶ֧חֶם תָּמִ֛יד לְפָנָ֖יו כָּל־יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he changed [the] clothes of his imprisonment, and he ate bread continually before him all [the] days of his life.
pieces: So Jehoiachin put off his prison clothes, and for the rest of his life he ate regularly at the king's table.

L.29: And he changed his prison clothes, and he ate bread continually before him all the days of his life.

R.29: Jehoiachin no longer had to wear prison clothes. For the rest of his life he ate his meals at the king's table.

decisions.choice: he changed: Jehoiachin changed his clothes
alternatives: the king changed his prison clothes
decisions.reason: The subject is most likely Jehoiachin, who put off his prison clothes; it could also be the king, who had them changed. Either way his time as a prisoner was over.

decisions.choice: ate bread before him: ate at the king's table
decisions.reason: To eat at the king's table was a mark of honor and of provision for life, as David gave Jonathan's son Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 9:7, 13) and the sons of Barzillai (1 Kings 2:7).

decisions.choice: all the days of his life: until Jehoiachin died
decisions.reason: The phrase looks to Jehoiachin's own life, and is repeated in verse 30. Jeremiah 52:33 has the same sentence.

decisions.choice: Jehoiachin; at the king's table (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jehoiachin and say "at the king's table" for "before him".

records.source: וַאֲרֻחָת֗וֹ אֲרֻחַ֨ת תָּמִ֧יד נִתְּנָה־לּ֛וֹ מֵאֵ֥ת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ דְּבַר־י֣וֹם בְּיוֹמ֑וֹ כֹּ֖ל יְמֵ֥י חַיָּֽו׃
records.gloss: And his allowance, an allowance continual, was given to him from with the king, [a] matter of [a] day in its day, all [the] days of his life.
pieces: And the king gave him a regular allowance, a portion for each day, all the days of his life.

L.30: And his allowance, a regular allowance, was given to him by the king, a day's portion each day, all the days of his life.

R.30: Every day the king gave him what he needed for that day, for the rest of his life.

decisions.choice: a day's portion each day: a daily share
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of a daily quota or ration (Exodus 5:13; 16:4). The king provided for him day by day.

decisions.choice: the allowance: royal rations
decisions.reason: Clay tablets from Nebuchadnezzar's palace in Babylon record rations of oil given to "Ya'ukin, king of the land of Yahud" and to his sons, which shows that Jehoiachin was already being supplied by the court years earlier.

decisions.choice: an open ending: the line of David is still alive
alternatives: a note only that the king lived on in exile
decisions.reason: The book does not end with the burning of the temple but with David's heir alive, freed and honored. The LORD had promised David a lasting house (2 Samuel 7:12-16) and had kept "a lamp" for David in Jerusalem (1 Kings 11:36; 2 Kings 8:19). The writer does not say what this means, but the ending leaves room for hope. Jehoiachin's grandson Zerubbabel would later lead the return from exile (1 Chronicles 3:17-19; Ezra 3:2; Haggai 2:23).

decisions.choice: Jeremiah 52:34: "until the day of his death"
decisions.reason: Jeremiah 52:34 has the same sentence and adds "until the day of his death" before "all the days of his life".

decisions.choice: the king gave him (Balanced, Readable); what he needed for that day (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make the king the subject instead of the passive "was given". Readable explains the allowance as what he needed each day.
